subject: Helix: cross-border egress scoping and annotated access map
messages:
From: Eva Carter <eva.carter@helixhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal - Helix Health <contracts@helixhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 17:15:00 +00:00
Subject: Cross-border data egress & access — need annotated map

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our DPA review and upcoming procurement checkpoint we need a concise, annotated view of how PII moves through Redwood’s stack for the Helix integration. Specifically can you provide:

- A dataflow diagram that highlights: which PII fields (email, patient_id, device_id) may leave the EU, and where they egress to (region/service).
- An access annotation: which internal roles and which subprocessors can access raw PII at each hop (read/write), plus whether access is supported via customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed keys.
- Any pseudonymization/tokenization that happens before egress and where derived artifacts (embeddings, hashes) are stored.
- Retention windows for raw vs tokenized data and for audit logs.

We’d also like to see an up-to-date subprocessor roster and confirmation if any analytics/observability logs contain PII fields in plain text. If you can attach an annotated SVG or PDF and a simple CSV access matrix that would be ideal.

Target for Helix procurement: Dec 22. If we can get a first pass by EOD PST Dec 20, we’ll route through Legal for a quick check.

Best,
Eva Carter
DPO, Helix Health

(Attachment: none)
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Eva Carter <eva.carter@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 18:03:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Cross-border data egress & access — need annotated map

Hi Eva — thanks for the clear list. We put together a first-pass annotated diagram and a simple access matrix and attached both. Quick notes up front:

- TL;DR: For hosted Redwood API (standard tenant model) raw PII submitted to the API is stored transiently in the serving region for inference, and persistent storage (logs, traces, debug artifacts) may be replicated to our US analytics region for monitoring unless you select EU-only residency in the Dedicated/Private options.
- KMS: By default we use Redwood-managed keys for hosted customers; customer-managed KMS is available on Redwood Private or via an enterprise-managed KMS integration (details in the attached notes).
- Pseudonymization: We do not automatically tokenise or fully pseudonymize raw text before tokenization/embedding — customers can enable tokenization pipelines during ingestion in Dedicated/Private. Embeddings and hashed metadata may be stored outside the EU depending on routing policy.
- Retention: Raw request payloads: 30 days (default, configurable for enterprise contracts). Embeddings/derived artifacts: 90 days default. Audit logs: 365 days.

Attachments included: redwood_egress_annotation_v1.svg (annotated dataflow), redwood_access_matrix_v2.csv (role/subprocessor access matrix). We’ve flagged items in the SVG where we think Helix will want explicit contractual controls (KMS custody, analytics replication).

A couple of clarifying Qs that will help tighten the diagram:
1) Which specific PII fields are in scope for Helix beyond email/patient_id/device_id? (e.g., free-text clinical notes, device telemetry that includes identifiers).
2) Do you require EU-residency only (no egress under any circumstance), or is egress allowed provided SCCs and technical controls are in place?
3) Any preferred subprocessor exclusions (e.g., ban certain cloud providers)?

We’ll update the diagram based on your answers and include an explicit line-by-line mapping to DPA Annex fields.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Senior Privacy Engineer
Redwood Inference

(Attachments: redwood_egress_annotation_v1.svg, redwood_access_matrix_v2.csv)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 21:30:00 +00:00
Subject: Fwd: Cross-border data egress — internal notes and suggested edits

Mina / Jonas — quick internal notes before we send the consolidated reply to Helix. Forwarding my quick markup.

Key edits to include in the next version:
- Mark AWS us-east-1 and GCP europe-west1 as the likely egress endpoints for hosted telemetry/analytics; clarify that inference kernels run in-region unless routing policy forces a fallback (we need to show fallback chain explicitly).
- Explicitly state that subprocessor roster includes: AWS (infrastructure), SusaLogs (observability), KeySafe (KMS proxy) — include PDF roster.
- For embeddings: call out the risk note that embeddings derived from PII are considered sensitive and may be treated as pseudonymized data but are reversible in aggregate (per our internal risk table) — recommend contractual handling.
- For logs: ensure we redact obvious PII keys in application logs by default, but traces may include truncated identifiers for debugging. Provide retention and redaction knobs in the access matrix.

I attached the latest subprocessor roster and an updated access matrix CSV with specific role names and read/write flags. I suggest we add a short paragraph offering Helix the Dedicated/Private option if they require strict EU-only custody and customer-managed KMS.

Marissa Cole
Lead Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

(Attachments: subprocessor_roster_Q42026.pdf, redwood_access_matrix_v2.csv)
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Eva Carter <eva.carter@helixhealth.com>, privacy-team@helixhealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Legal - Helix Health <contracts@helixhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 14:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Cross-border data egress & access — final answers + artifacts

Hi Eva and team,

Thanks — covered below is a concise mapping back to your original asks and the artifacts we attached. If you'd like, we can walk through these on a 30-minute call tomorrow morning PST.

1) Which PII fields may egress and where
- In scope (examples): email, patient_id, device_id, and free-text clinical notes when submitted.
- Hosted (default): inference requests are processed in the request region; derived artifacts (embeddings, logs) may be replicated to our analytics region (US) unless you choose EU-only residency via Dedicated/Private. See diagram: redwood_egress_annotation_v1.svg (nodes annotated with region codes).

2) Access annotation (who can access raw PII)
- Internal roles: Platform SRE (limited to debugging with JIT escalation), Model Ops (access to persisted derived artifacts for retraining), Security (access to audit logs). Read/write flags are in redwood_access_matrix_v2.csv.
- Subprocessors: AWS (infra — hosts compute & storage), SusaLogs (observability/retention), KeySafe (KMS proxy for Redwood-managed keys). Full roster: subprocessor_roster_Q42026.pdf.

3) KMS and key custody
- Hosted customers: Redwood-managed KMS by default (KeySafe).
- Enterprise options: customer-managed KMS available with Dedicated/Private (bring-your-own-key integrations supported).

4) Pseudonymization/tokenization
- Default hosted flow: we do not tokenise free-text before inference. Customers can enable tokenization pipelines on Dedicated/Private deployments; we can also provide guidance on pre-ingest pseudonymization. Embeddings and hashed metadata are considered derived artifacts and are retained per the retention table.

5) Retention windows
- Raw request payloads: 30 days (configurable in contract).
- Embeddings/derived artifacts: 90 days default.
- Audit logs: 365 days. All retention parameters can be tightened via Dedicated/Private terms.

6) Logs & observability
- Application logs redact known PII keys by default. Traces may include truncated identifiers for debugging. We recommend contractual language that prohibits use of logs for profiling without explicit consent; we can provide a log-redaction sample in the DPA Annex.

Attachments (first-pass):
- redwood_egress_annotation_v1.svg (annotated dataflow with region & subprocessor notes)
- redwood_access_matrix_v2.csv (role/subprocessor read/write flags, redaction knobs)
- subprocessor_roster_Q42026.pdf (current roster & regions)

Next steps: please confirm the specific PII fields to lock into the Annex (if different from examples above) and whether Helix requires EU-residency-only. If EU-only is required, we’ll prepare a Dedicated/Private proposal with customer-managed KMS and a tailored retention schedule.

Call options: I’m available Mon 08:00–11:00 PST / Tue 16:00–18:00 CET. Suggest a 30-min sync with Legal + DPO.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Privacy Engineer
Redwood Inference
